content: Raltegravir, commonly known by the brand name Isentress, is a medication used in combination with other antiretroviral drugs to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, which helps the immune system function more effectively. This reduction in viral load decreases the risk of developing complications associated with HIV, such as opportunistic infections and certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Raltegravir belongs to a class of drugs called integrase inhibitors, which block the action of the HIV enzyme integrase, preventing the virus from replicating. It is important to note that raltegravir is not a cure for HIV infection. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, patients should continue taking all prescribed HIV medications exactly as directed by their healthcare provider. Additionally, the use of effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity is recommended. Patients should avoid sharing personal items that may come into contact with blood or bodily fluids, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors. Before starting raltegravir, patients should read the patient information leaflet provided by their pharmacist and consult their healthcare provider for any questions. The dosage of raltegravir is determined based on the patient’s medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications they may be taking. The medication should be swallowed whole, as directed by the manufacturer. While some similar drugs can be split or crushed, this should not be done with raltegravir unless specifically instructed by a healthcare provider. Patients should avoid using antacids containing aluminum or magnesium while taking this medication, as these can interfere with its effectiveness. Adherence to the prescribed regimen is critical for the medication to work effectively. Patients should not increase their dose, take the drug more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Similarly, they should not reduce the dose or stop taking raltegravir or other HIV medications without consulting their doctor, even for a short period. For optimal results, the medication should be taken at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects of raltegravir include headache, nausea, and difficulty sleeping. Patients should remember that their doctor has prescribed this medication because the benefits outweigh the potential risks. As the immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off previously undetected infections, which could cause symptoms of these infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, leading to symptoms that require medical attention. These reactions can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking raltegravir, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdomen or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not fully understood. Serious allergic reactions to raltegravir are rare but require immediate medical attention if they occur. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects, and patients should contact their doctor for medical advice if they experience any concerning symptoms. Before taking raltegravir, patients should inform their doctor or pharmacist if they have any allergies, including to raltegravir itself, or if they have any other medical conditions. The medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, raltegravir should only be used when clearly needed, as it may be part of a treatment plan to reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to the baby. Raltegravir can pass into breast milk, so patients should discuss breastfeeding with their healthcare provider. Drug interactions may alter how raltegravir or other medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Patients should keep a list of all the products they use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share this information with their doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions, so patients should consult their healthcare provider for more information. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, emergency services should be contacted immediately by calling 911. Otherwise, a poison control center should be contacted right away. In the United States, the poison control hotline is 1-800-222-1222. Patients taking raltegravir should undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, to monitor their response to treatment. It is essential to keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as the patient remembers. However, if it is close to the time for the next dose, the missed dose should be skipped, and the next dose should be taken at the regular time. Patients should not double the dose to catch up. Raltegravir should be stored in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. It should not be stored in the bathroom. The drying agent (desiccant) included in the bottle should be kept inside to maintain the medication’s stability. The bottle should be tightly closed when not in use. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless instructed to do so. Expired or no longer needed medications should be properly discarded according to local disposal guidelines. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about raltegravir. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for every individual. Patients should always consult their healthcare provider for complete information about this product and their specific health needs.
